epic.title: EPIC-24: Top Concepts - Verbatim Source Attribution
epic.functionalNeed:
The "Top Concepts Associated with Your Brand" panel must attribute each concept to the sources that genuinely support it, and assign each concept a sentiment that reflects what those sources actually say about the brand. Today both the attribution and the sentiment are produced by an after-the-fact guess that the user cannot trust as proof.
The Top Concepts panel shows each concept with a sentiment and a list of supporting sources. Today the analysis collects sources and concepts separately, then a secondary step tries to guess, after the fact, which source backs which concept and which sentiment. That guessing step has three failure modes the user can see: a source is attributed to a concept it does not actually discuss; a source that never mentions the brand still appears under a concept; and a concept's sentiment is inferred rather than evidenced, so the user cannot verify why a concept reads positive, mixed, or negative. The result is that the "Click on a concept to view sources" experience cannot be fully trusted as proof, which undermines the whole panel for a user trying to understand and defend their brand perception.
The binding between a concept and its supporting sources, and the sentiment assigned to each concept, must reflect what the cited sources actually say about the brand rather than an after-the-fact guess. This is achieved by asking each AI engine to return its concepts with the supporting sources nested directly inside each concept, so every source sits under the concept the engine actually used it for and there is no separate step guessing which source backs which concept (see Requested output schema below). Everything else stays the same: the brand ranking shape, the source-typing rules, the sentiment dimensions, the channel and publisher fields, and the existing source fields.
---
> Exception: this analysis normally describes behavior only, with no schemas or field names in the body. The schema below is included deliberately because the nesting of sources inside concepts is the change this analysis delivers, so the requested shape is the requirement, not an implementation detail.
The analysis asks each AI engine to return its concepts with their supporting sources nested inside each concept, rather than as a separate flat list bound afterward:
scope: - Capturing or displaying verbatim passages attached to each source - out of scope for this analysis.
- The Top Concepts panel layout, the sentiment distribution bar, and the sort and filter controls - unchanged.
- The concept list itself (which concepts surface, frequency ordering) - unchanged except that attribution and sentiment become trustworthy.
- The other analysis surfaces (brand rankings, win rate, visibility) - unchanged.
- Re-analysis of existing analyses. Analyses produced before this fix keep their old attribution until re-run. Whether to backfill or only apply forward is a product decision.

stories.title: 24-4 — Concepts Render When One Engine Returns Nothing (US 1.4)
stories.userStory:
## In plain terms

Now that **every** engine (not just Gemini) must return concepts, a weaker engine might occasionally return a broken or empty answer. This story makes sure that if one engine returns nothing usable, the **Top Concepts panel still shows the concepts from the other engines** instead of going blank. It also keeps **old reports** (created before this change) displaying correctly during the rollout.
stories.acceptanceCriteria: **AC1** — Given one AI engine returns no usable sources for a given analysis type, When the Top Concepts panel renders, Then concepts still render from the engines that did return sources, and the panel is not blanked by the one engine returning nothing.

stories.title: 24-3 — Preserve the Existing Analysis Shape, No Regression (US 1.3)
stories.userStory:
## In plain terms

This is the **safety net**. It guarantees that improving the concept attribution (24.1) and sentiment (24.2) does **NOT** change anything else: brand rankings, source typing, the Citation Sources graph, and every non-perception chart stay exactly as they are. The backend storage shape and the API contract are kept identical → the **frontend renders unchanged**.
stories.acceptanceCriteria: **AC1** — Given the attribution change, When the analysis completes, Then the brand ranking shape, source-typing, sentiment dimensions, and existing source fields (`url`, `title`, `publisher`, `date`, `channel`) are **unchanged** from before the fix.

stories.title: 24-2 — Evidenced Concept Sentiment (US 1.2)
stories.userStory:
## In plain terms

A concept's sentiment (positive / mixed / negative) is currently **inferred from the whole answer** by the second AI step. This story makes the sentiment come **straight from the engine, grounded in that concept's own sources**. The engine returns **both** a label (positive/mixed/negative) **and a numeric score** per concept — so the Sentiment KPI keeps the same granularity it has today.
stories.acceptanceCriteria: **AC1** — Given a concept's sentiment (positive, mixed, or negative), When it is computed, Then it reflects what the attributed sources say about the brand, carried with the concept — rather than being inferred from the answer as a whole.

stories.title: 24-1 — Trustworthy Concept-Source Attribution (US 1.1)
stories.userStory:
## In plain terms

Today, when a user clicks a concept in "Top Concepts" and sees its sources, those sources were **guessed after the fact** by a second AI step — and a bug attaches **every** source of an answer to **every** concept of that answer, so sources appear under concepts they don't discuss. This story makes **each AI engine return its concepts with the supporting sources already attached**, and removes the bug → the source list under a concept becomes trustworthy proof.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1** — Given an analysis runs, When an AI engine returns its concepts, Then each concept includes its own supporting sources nested in the response, rather than a separate flat source list bound afterward.

**AC2** — Given the Top Concepts panel, When concepts are derived, Then each concept is attributed only to sources that actually discuss it, with no source attached on an inferred or guessed binding.

**AC3** — Given a source that does not mention the brand, When the user views any concept, Then that source does not appear under the concept.
